target_title: Base64 from Apache Commons Codec 1.3 (2005, real open-source code)

mutants.quirk: Decoding silently skips every non-Base64 character (spaces, line breaks, junk) instead of rejecting it
Chunked output separates lines with CRLF (\r\n), not LF
Chunked output always ends with a line separator, even for short input
isArrayByteBase64 treats whitespace as valid Base64

modernizations.goal: Bring this class up to modern Java 21: generics instead of raw collections, java.time instead of Calendar, StringBuilder, no deprecated APIs. Behaviour must stay exactly the same.

Ticket SEC-118 (tech debt): we still ship our own Base64 implementation from 2005, but Java has had java.util.Base64 since Java 8. Reimplement this class on top of java.util.Base64 so we stop maintaining a hand-rolled encoder, and modernize the rest to Java 21. Keep the public API.
